evals.name: budget-rule-explainer
evals.prompt: I teach personal finance on YouTube. I want to make a ~5 minute video explaining the 50/30/20 budget rule for people in their first job. It's just me, I film at home on a Samsung phone, I have maybe $60 to spend and 10 days. I don't want it to be a boring talking head. Can you direct it for me? Show me visually how the whole video will look, what I'll use, what it'll cost and how to make each part.
evals.expected_output: A director's board (HTML) with vision, beat timeline covering 5 minutes, diagram storyboard frames, A/V script, per-shot method and steps, tools and tiered budget within $60, feasibility ratings with fallbacks, workflow over 10 days, assumptions.
expectations: A visual board file (HTML) is delivered
The board has at least 6 storyboard frames drawn as diagrams
There is a picture/sound script with timecodes
The structure (beats) covers the full ~5 minute runtime
Every shot states a method and how-to steps
Tools are listed with costs and a budget total that fits $60 in at least one tier
Every shot has a feasibility rating and every risky shot has a fallback
Assumptions are stated
Prices are marked as approximate or dated
A workflow or schedule fits the 10-day deadline
Storyboard frames show the mood or look (color, light or grade), not only grey layout shapes
The user can watch the sequence play in time (an animatic or moving mock-up)
Every number quoted in the chat reply (runtime, totals, shares, counts) matches the plan files
On-camera talking-head share is under half of the runtime, measured from the shot list
A thumbnail concept is included

evals.name: candle-reel-ad
evals.prompt: Plan a 30-second Instagram Reel ad for my small handmade soy candle brand 'Ember & Oak'. It's just me and my phone, no crew. I'm thinking of using AI video for a dreamy forest scene with my candle glowing on a mossy log. Budget is under ₹8,000 (I'm in India). Show me visually how it'll look, what tools, the cost and how to pull it off.
evals.expected_output: A 9:16 director's board with a hook in the first 1-2 seconds, honest AI feasibility (product consistency, text), a hybrid approach (real candle filmed, AI or practical forest), costs in rupees under 8,000, fallbacks.
expectations: A visual board file (HTML) is delivered
Storyboard frames are vertical (9:16)
Costs are given in rupees and at least one tier is under ₹8,000
The plan warns that AI video struggles to keep the real candle/label consistent
The plan films the real candle (e.g. tabletop moss set or composite) rather than relying on AI to generate the product
The hook lands in the first 1-3 seconds
Every shot has a feasibility rating and risky shots have fallbacks
AI or music licensing/disclosure is addressed
Storyboard frames show the mood or look (color, light or grade), not only grey layout shapes
The user can watch the sequence play in time (an animatic or moving mock-up)
Every number quoted in the chat reply (runtime, totals, shares, counts) matches the plan files
The real candle is on screen within the first 2 seconds

evals.name: fix-drone-opening
evals.prompt: I'm making a 90-second brand film for my small architecture studio. The opening shot in my plan was a drone flying over the city at sunset and then pushing into our office window on the 12th floor, where the team is working. I don't have a drone, flying is banned in our area, and when I tried Runway and Kling the buildings kept bending and melting. What else can I do so the opening still works?
evals.expected_output: Fix mode: names the opening's job, diagnoses blockers, at least 3 ranked alternatives with cost/effort/fidelity, a clear recommendation, fixes for AI warping, and a visual of the new opening.
expectations: States what the opening shot must achieve (its job/intent)
Offers at least 3 distinct alternatives
Makes one clear recommendation with a reason
Compares options on cost and effort or fidelity
Gives specific techniques to stop AI warping (e.g. image-to-video from a still, slow/short moves, 2.5D parallax)
Mentions a permission/licensing point for the alternatives (stock licence, attribution, building access)
Delivers a visual of the new opening (storyboard frames or board)
Every number quoted in the chat reply (runtime, totals, shares, counts) matches the plan files
Explains why the AI tools warped the buildings, in plain words
